newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt, small businesses agree on tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt, small businesses agree on tax bill.

text.p: The Brazilian government and representatives of the country's small business sector reached an agreement on a new single tax for small and micro-sized companies, a deputy in charge of the bill said.

The bill, which was due to be put to a vote in the lower house later on Tuesday, would set a three percent federal corporate tax for companies earning up to 60,000 reais annually, deputy Paulo Bauer told reporters.
Firms with an annual turnover of up to 90,000 reais would pay four percent, while those earning up to 120,000 reais would pay five percent, he said.
Small companies may also opt to pay their state and municipal taxes in association with the new federal tax which has been dubbed the "simple one."
Representatives of small businesses say they expect the total tax paid by small companies will range between three and eight percent according to their turnover.

The government had been recommending that the federal tax be set at between five and 7.5 percent, which would have meant a total tax payment of five to 10 percent by small companies, but representatives of the sector argued that rate was too high.
